Parvati.description: A young girl who admires Devdas and is his close companion; she is the daughter of Nilkontho Chokrovorty and later becomes the wife of Bhubon Chowdhury.

Govind Pandit.description: The schoolmaster, responsible for maintaining discipline at the village school.

Bhulonath.description: A village boy who assists in the school and keeps an eye on Devdas.

Narayan Mukherjee.description: Narayan Mukherjee is Devdas's father, a respected and strict man in the village whose death precipitates the events of the chapter.

Nilkontho Chokrovorty.description: Nilkontho Chokrovorty is Parvati's father, a comfortably well-off landowner and neighbor to Narayan Mukherjee, who opposes the custom of bride-price.

Dharmadas.description: A servant employed by Narayan Mukherjee to look after Devdas since childhood.

Monu.description: A child in the village who talks with Parvati about Devdas's absence from school.

Baishakh.description: The first month of the Bengali calendar, corresponding to April-May, marking the start of summer.

Mukherjee.description: Mukherjee refers to the family of Devdas and Dwijdas, a prominent Bengali Brahmin family whose estate, Mookherjee manor, serves as a central setting.

Chokrovorty.description: A Bengali surname, here referring to Parvati's family.

banyan.description: A type of large, spreading tree native to India, often found in village commons.

Pandit.description: An honorific for a learned man or teacher, commonly used for Brahmin scholars.

annas.description: A former unit of Indian currency, equal to 1/16 of a rupee.

gondas.description: A small unit of currency, historically used in India, equal to 1/64 of a rupee.

whitewash.description: A mixture used for painting walls, often made from powdered lime.

satchel.description: A small bag, typically used by schoolchildren to carry books and food.

Devdas.description: The protagonist, a young boy known for his impulsive and rebellious nature, son of Narayan Mukherjee.

Sir.description: A colonial-era term used by students to address their teacher respectfully.

Squire.description: A British colonial term for a local landowner or authority figure, used here to denote a person of status.

Monoroma.description: Paru's friend who lives further away and attends school.

Monoroma’s aunt.description: The aunt of Monoroma, who answers the door when Paru visits.

Roshik Pal.description: The owner of a store that Paru visits.

Vaishnovi.description: A group of three female singers Paru encounters, who sing devotional songs.

Roshik Pal’s store.description: A local shop owned by Roshik Pal, visited by Paru.

auntie.description: Auntie (or auntie) is a respectful or affectionate term for an older woman, often used for a mother's friend or neighbor.

alms.description: Charitable donations, often given to religious mendicants or performers.

gonds.description: A small denomination of currency used in colonial India.

kora.description: A minor coin or currency unit in colonial India, smaller than an anna.

Nogen.description: A cousin of Devdas’s mother who lives in Calcutta and agrees to host Devdas.

Parvati’s mother.description: Parvati’s mother is a caring and supportive woman, questioning and disciplining Parvati after incidents and supporting her daughter's wishes.

Parvati’s grandmother.description: Parvati’s grandmother is a protective and outspoken figure in the household, defending Parvati and greeting Devdas affectionately.

Calcutta.description: A major city in colonial India (now Kolkata), representing urban sophistication and education.

Tal Shonapur.description: Tal Shonapur (also spelled Tal-Sonapur) is the village or estate referenced as Parvati's and Devdas's ancestral home, symbolizing rural Bengal.

Ma.description: A Bengali and Hindi word meaning 'mother', used as an affectionate address.

Devdas’ mother.description: Devdas's mother, a caring and concerned woman who plays a significant role in shaping Devdas's future.

Burdwan.description: A region in Bengal, referenced as the location of the wealthy bridegroom's estate.

bride-price.description: A sum of money or property paid by the groom's family to the bride's family as part of the marriage arrangement.

Mono.description: A diminutive or affectionate nickname for Monoroma.

Kishan Singh.description: The old gatekeeper at the manor house, found dozing with a book of scriptures in his lap.

Ramayana.description: An ancient Indian epic, considered a sacred scripture, recounting the life and adventures of Lord Rama.

Choonilal.description: A perennial student and Devdas's friend in Calcutta, known for his late-night outings and jovial demeanor.

B.A..description: Bachelor of Arts, a university degree reflecting the colonial-era education system.

Hathopotha.description: A place name, the estate or region associated with Parvati's bridegroom, the Zamindar.

Shubho Drishti.description: A Bengali wedding ritual where the bride and groom look into each other's eyes for the first time during the ceremony.

Sri.description: A respectful honorific prefix used before names in India.

bridegroom.description: An archaic or formal term for a man on his wedding day.

choker.description: A close-fitting necklace, part of traditional bridal jewelry.

Great Mother.description: A reverential reference to a goddess or divine mother figure, invoked in times of distress.

Chondromookhi.description: A courtesan in the Chitpore district who meets Devdas and is affected by his unusual behavior; she later moves to Oshothjhuri.

Eden Gardens.description: A famous park in Calcutta (now Kolkata), known for its scenic beauty and later for its cricket stadium.

Chitpore.description: A historic district in Calcutta, known for its cultural significance and as a location for courtesan houses.

mess hall.description: A communal dining area, often used in boarding houses or institutions.

Mohendro.description: Parvati's eldest stepson, a graceful young man who welcomes her and helps mediate family relationships.

Joshoda.description: Parvati's stepdaughter, initially angry and estranged, but reconciles with Parvati after being shown kindness.

Bhubon Chowdhury.description: Parvati's husband, a wealthy zamindar of Hathipota preoccupied with his estates and saddened by his family's fragmentation.

Binode Lal.description: Bhubon's youngest son, who returns home after his examinations and is cared for by Parvati.

zamindar.description: A zamindar is a hereditary landowner during colonial India, often wealthy and influential; 'Zamindar' is the capitalized form.

in-laws.description: A term referring to the family of one's spouse, commonly used in Indian English.

Chondromookhi’s house.description: The residence of Chondromookhi, a courtesan, which serves as a significant setting for Devdas's visits.

Modhusudon Ghoshe.description: A villager or family acquaintance who tries to comfort Devdas after the funeral.

lakhs.description: A unit in the Indian numbering system equal to one hundred thousand (100,000).

sari.description: A traditional garment worn by women in South Asia, consisting of a long piece of cloth draped around the body.

conch.description: A large seashell used as a wind instrument in Hindu rituals, often sounded to mark the beginning of prayers.

Catermonie.description: A friend or acquaintance of Chondromookhi in Calcutta who assists her and receives her paintings.

Benaras.description: A holy city in India, also known as Varanasi, renowned for its religious significance and as a place of pilgrimage.

bangle.description: A bangle is a rigid bracelet, typically made of metal, glass, or plastic, worn around the wrist; 'bangles' is the plural form, common in South Asian cultures.

pawnbroker.description: A person or business that lends money at interest in exchange for personal property as collateral, common in colonial-era India.

Jolodbala.description: Mohendro's wife, intelligent and efficient, who becomes upset about Parvati's household spending.

Mother Ganga.description: A reverential term for the Ganges River, considered sacred in Hinduism.

Annapurna.description: A Hindu goddess of nourishment, with whom Parvati is compared.

zamindari.description: A term referring to a large landowning estate, often under the control of a zamindar (landlord) in colonial India.

sepoy.description: An Indian soldier serving under British or other colonial command.

pyre.description: A pile of wood used for burning a dead body as part of a funeral rite.

kool-tree.description: A type of tree, likely referring to the Indian jujube (Ziziphus mauritiana), common in Bengal.

Jom.description: The Bengali name for Yama, the Hindu god of death.

Bhoirov.description: A farmer in Oshothjhuri, devoted to Chondromookhi, who assists her with errands and travel.

Roma Bagchi.description: A villager whose daughter helps Chondromookhi maintain her courtyard.

Bindu.description: A servant or attendant in the Zamindar's household, called by the lady of the manor.

Nindu.description: Another servant or attendant in the Zamindar's household.

Kebla Ram.description: Bhoirov's son, who accompanies Chondromookhi to Calcutta and helps her settle there.

Doyal.description: A pawnbroker in Calcutta who helps Chondromookhi with money and finding a new residence.

Oshothjhuri.description: Oshothjhuri is a village where Chondromookhi resides after leaving the city; 'Oshoth' refers to the sacred Ashvattha or peepal tree, likely giving the village its name.

Elahabad.description: A city in India (now Allahabad/Prayagraj), mentioned as a place Chondromookhi claims to have visited.

Mr. Dewan.description: The accountant or steward in the Zamindar's household, responsible for financial matters.

veranda.description: A veranda (or verandah) is a roofed, open-air porch or gallery attached to the outside of a building, common in Indian architecture.

courtyard.description: An open space surrounded by buildings or walls, typical in Indian homes.

tulsi.description: Holy basil, a sacred plant in Hindu tradition, often grown in courtyards.

pan.description: A preparation of betel leaf chewed with areca nut and other ingredients, common in India.

shawl.description: A piece of fabric worn over the shoulders, often for warmth or modesty.

ox-cart.description: A cart pulled by oxen, used for rural transportation in India.

flannel.description: A soft woven fabric, here used as a wrap for warmth or comfort.

arrears.description: Unpaid or overdue debts, especially rent.

gilt jewelry.description: Jewelry coated with a thin layer of gold.

tenants.description: People who rent land or property from a landlord.

gentlefolk.description: A term for people of high social status or refinement.

tithe.description: A tax or levy, often a portion of agricultural produce, paid to a landlord or the state.

Dwijdas Mookherjee.description: Dwijdas Mookherjee is Devdas's older brother, deeply affected by their father's death and involved in managing the family's finances.

Lahore.description: A historic city in present-day Pakistan, visited by Devdas.

Bombay.description: A major city on India's west coast, now called Mumbai.

Jaistha.description: A month in the Bengali calendar, corresponding roughly to May-June.

Bhadro.description: A month in the Bengali calendar, corresponding roughly to August-September.

Patna.description: A city in eastern India, capital of Bihar.

Pandua.description: A town in Bengal, near Hathipota.

Hathipota.description: A fictional or local village, home to Parvati.

Chondal.description: Chondal refers to a marginalized tribal community in Bengal, often tasked with menial or 'unclean' work; 'Chondals' are members of this group.

palanquin.description: A palanquin is a covered litter carried by bearers, used for transporting people; 'palanquins' is the plural form, used as a mode of transport for the wealthy or noble.

rupee.description: The rupee is the currency of India, with 'rupees' as the plural and 'rs.' as the abbreviation.

sapphire.description: A precious blue gemstone, here referring to a ring worn by Devdas.

sacred thread.description: A symbolic thread worn by upper-caste Hindu males after a coming-of-age ceremony.

Brahmin.description: A member of the Hindu priestly caste.

Devi.description: An honorific meaning 'goddess' or 'respected lady', used for women.

sir.description: A respectful form of address, often used in colonial and post-colonial India.
